newsitem.title: USA: MGE spring wheat ends mostly lower on hedging.
newsitem.headline: MGE spring wheat ends mostly lower on hedging.

text.p: MGE spring wheat futures ended mostly lower Friday, pressured by hedging, competitive world wheat prices and a private U.S. wheat production forecast that was above USDA's August estimate, traders said.
Losses appeared to have been limited in part, by significant flour mill-type buying.
"There's a lot of selling of Dec linked to more country movement," a MGE trader said at the midsession.
Memphis-based analytical firm Sparks was reported to have pegged total 1996/97 wheat production at 2.33 billion bushels, above USDA's August estimate of 2.249 billion.
MGE spring wheat closed 10-3/4 cents per bushel lower to two cents higher, with Dec down five cents at $4.29-1/4. Sept shed 10-3/4 cents to close at $4.46-1/4.
Wilson was reported to have sold 1.8 million Dec bushels. General Mills bought two million Dec and LFG bought 1.5 million Dec, traders said.
The MGE estimated Friday's spring wheat futures volume at 22.20 billion bushels, versus 28.675 on Thursday.
MGE barley futures closed unchanged to three cents per cwt lower, with Sept unchanged at $7.40 per cwt.
